newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac props up embattled Juppe with unity display.
newsitem.headline: Chirac props up embattled Juppe with unity display.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac put on a display of unity with his embattled Prime Minister Alain Juppe as criticism of government policy from within the centre-right ruling coalition intensified.
At a Franco-British summit in the southwestern city of Bordeaux, Chirac showed his confidence in Juppe by including him in every meeting with British Prime Minister John Major.

He also took Juppe, who as Bordeaux mayor is the summit's official host, with him on Friday morning to meet a crowd of supporters who cried "Chirac-Juppe" and "Stick with Juppe" outside the city hall.

Juppe, whose popularity has plunged amid record unemployment, has faced growing criticism from within his fractious coalition over his drive to cut the state deficit in order to help qualify for a planned European Union single currency by 1999.
During a meeting with local parliamentarians on Thursday, Chirac -- with Juppe at his side -- rejected calls for a change in direction, saying: "No other policy is possible."
The display of solidarity followed new calls from within his coalition for Chirac to dump his prime minister.
Senior party colleague and ex-interior minister Charles Pasqua earlier this week blasted Juppe for bringing France toward collapse and revolution.

Pasqua's attack followed reports that his former fellow anti-Maastricht campaigner Philippe Seguin, the Gaullist speaker of the National Assembly, had drafted an alternative government platform, shifting emphasis from cutting deficits to fighting unemployment, in case Chirac sacked Juppe.

Concern has been growing in the ruling coalition that social discontent may result in the Socialists returning to power at the next general election scheduled in 1998. The centre-right took power from the Socialists in 1993.
Francois Leotard, the leader of the Union for French Democracy (UDF), the junior partner in the ruling coalition, said Juppe's days as prime minister appeared numbered.

"Chirac is aware of Juppe's deficiencies. He knows he must (change prime ministers). In his mind, it's clear," Leotard told the daily Le Figaro. "If we continue this way, we'll be beaten in the legislative elections."
